ledger.claim: The rider clears the identity limb of her burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00526, and trip_record.started_at (2026-09-14T23:36:40+08:00) coincides with the trace's first fix, so the three artifacts describe one and the same trip and the ride can be measured on the record as it stands.

The driver's own trace is complete: 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so it satisfies none of the impairment limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07. The rider's case therefore cannot be answered with a data-failure defence, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises out of this trace.

The rider's profile carries no citable adverse signal: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition that would require corroboration beyond the gps_trace (four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated) simply does not fire, and no other field on this profile may be used against the rider under POL-GEN-01.

Nothing in the bundle can excuse any part of what the rider was charged. There is no traffic advisory at all: EV-ADVIS-00526-01 is MISSING, status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no advisory names a road the optimal route traverses and the POL-RD-03 exoneration route is closed. The trip's chat log is likewise empty (message_count 0), so no rider-requested detour exists to invoke under POL-RD-04. I disclose the missing advisory's weight of 0.0 as POL-GEN-02(1) requires; its absence is itself citable.

The heart of the rider's complaint is the pricing mode, and the platform's own record proves it: trip_record.optimal_route_source records that the rider 'selected RYDE_X, display "up to 26.00"' and that the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI, while the fare_breakdown records fare_model METERED on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI with quoted_fare_sgd null, and the chat log holds no message evidencing any agreement to a metered taxi. The rider chose a product shown with a maximum price and was priced on a taxi meter she never selected. She does not assert a material distance deviation — the trace excess is 0.17 km, about 1.09%, under the POL-RD-01 gate — but the metered basis itself is what she disputes, and under POL-RD-11 the fare model governs which remedy is even available.

The two fare-model routes in this policy cannot be run cleanly on this record, which is precisely the situation POL-RD-10 exists for. POL-RD-11 requires fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd to be non-null and it is null, so the clause is invoked against a cited artifact that lacks the field the clause requires; POL-RD-02 runs only on a METERED trip once a deviation is established; and the record simultaneously supports a capped RYDE_X selection and a metered RYDE_TAXI dispatch, two mutually contradictory accounts of what was bought. With the required field absent and the evidence contradictory, and with no confident ruling available on the pricing basis, the case must ESCALATE under POL-RD-10, with the disputed amount held rather than collected.

POL-RD-01 sets two cumulative gates and neither is met on this trip's own evidence. The governing trace figure is 15.77 km against a booked optimal of 15.6 km — an excess of 0.17 km and 1.09% — far below the 0.8 km absolute threshold and the 20% proportional threshold. The derived deviation block records the status as 'no deviation'. Both establishment tests fail, so no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, because the latter is a rounded convenience copy. The trace governs at 15.77 km. Even the rounded 15.8 km copy yields an excess of roughly 0.2 km against a 15.6 km optimal — still nowhere near the 0.8 km and 20% gates. The rider fails both limbs on either reading, and the threshold is not close.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): coverage is 100.0%, there are 169 fixes at a 10 second cadence, the gaps list is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so there is no gap over 90 seconds, no 500 m straight-line jump and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. There is therefore no corroboration requirement under POL-RD-07(ii) and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3). The rider's excess figures rest on a clean, complete, unimpaired trace.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it: she must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, and the admissible, unimpaired evidence shows an excess of 0.17 km and 1.09%. Her claim text cites no evidence ID at all, and an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. Nothing in the bundle identifies a deviation for the driver to answer.

POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01' and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it. No deviation is established here, so the recomputation is not triggered and no distance-or-time refund arises. For completeness the ledger's own arithmetic block caps the exposure even on the rider's best counterfactual: charged_total 24.29 against a recomputed fare of 22.46 gives a refund of 1.85, which is 7.53% of the charged amount and does not approach the 90% FULL_REFUND share. The driver's fare is not exposed to any material adjustment on this record.

There is no billing-integrity defect to correct under POL-RD-09. The ERPs and tolls line is 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, the airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and every charge line is traceable to the metered rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI: base fare 3.80, distance fare 11.85, time fare 7.84 and platform fee 0.80 summing to the 24.29 charged. There is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no standalone pass-through correction is available under POL-RD-09(4).

The rider's real grievance is the product she was dispatched, not the route taken. The trip record shows she selected RYDE_X with the display 'up to 26.00' and the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI; the ledger records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null. POL-RD-11's upfront-quote remedy — the only route to a distance-and-time refund on a quote-model trip — is therefore unavailable on this record. In any event the charged total is 24.29, which is below the 26.00 cap the rider says she chose, and no line of the ledger produces the 46.50 figure in her claim. The driver's own statement that the meter is the fare and that the platform sent him the booking is consistent with the ledger and the trip record.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 and his completed_trips_90d is 250, so neither limb of the pattern test is met. Accordingly there is no FULL_REFUND uplift against the driver and no driver-conduct referral on this trip. I do not rely on the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, which POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the trailing-90-day figure.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver — this dispute is decided on the platform's own trip records, and no money moves.

1) No route deviation. The governing GPS trace records 15.77 km (EV-GPS-00526) against a booked optimal route of 15.6 km (EV-TRIP-00526) between the same pickup and drop-off. That is an excess of 0.17 km, or 1.09%. POL-RD-01 requires an excess both greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% before a deviation is established. Neither gate is met, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-02, the optimal-route fare recomputation, never runs. The trace is also unimpaired on this trip: 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, an empty gap list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so this is not a data-failure case and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation follows from the trace. For completeness only, had a deviation existed, the recomputed fare would have been SGD 22.46 against the SGD 24.29 charged, a difference of SGD 1.85 (well under the 90% full-refund share) — but that computation is not reached.

2) No billing-integrity defect. The SGD 24.29 charged (EV-FARE-00526) is base fare 3.80 + distance fare 11.85 + time fare 7.84 + platform fee 0.80, all on metered rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI. ERP and tolls are 0.00 with no gantries, and there is no airport surcharge. There is no phantom line for POL-RD-09(4) to refund, and therefore no 'billing integrity' referral.

3) Rider's product point. I accept the facts you relied on: the trip record shows you selected RYDE_X with the display 'up to 26.00' and that the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI (EV-TRIP-00526), while the ledger prices the trip on the meter (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null, EV-FARE-00526). But the fare you were charged, SGD 24.29, is below the SGD 26.00 maximum you say you chose, so there is no overcharge on this trip to refund; and the figure of SGD 46.50 in your claim appears in no record. POL-RD-11 governs capped/upfront-quoted fares and applies only where fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null. This trip was metered, so POL-RD-11 is inapplicable and supplies no remedy. It is not 'a clause invoked against an artifact lacking the field it requires' within POL-RD-10(5): it fails on the fare model itself, so no escalation follows from it.

4) Rider's escalation argument rejected. The POL-RD-10 triggers do not fire: the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and ledger; the timestamps are consistent; the trace is unimpaired; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or field-deficient artifact (no party asserts a traffic cause, the chat log is empty, and no amendment is claimed); and there is no pair of admissible, mutually contradictory accounts of comparable strength — the driver's statement that the meter is the fare and that the platform sent the booking is consistent with the ledger. Confidence here is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. This is a case to decide, not to hold.

5) Driver's points. I accept that no repeat-deviation pattern is established: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 250, so POL-RD-06 gives no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c). The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not used against anyone; it is context only under POL-GEN-01. I also accept that the rider's identity limb under POL-RD-08 is met, that her profile carries no citable adverse signal, and that no traffic advisory exists to excuse any part of the route.

Outcome. The route-deviation claim is not supported by the evidence, the fare charged is below the cap the rider cites, and no clause of the route-deviation policy provides a refund on these facts. The present state stands: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left as they are. If the rider wishes to pursue the separate question whether the platform should have honoured the RYDE_X product she selected rather than dispatching a taxi, that is a product-substitution matter outside this policy and is not resolved here.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
